external_sources.title: Food Standards Agency: Providing food at community and charity events
external_sources.supports: Safe preparation, storage and service need planning. Keep current ingredient and allergen information available. A school event proposal is not approval to serve food.

external_sources.title: Food Standards Agency: Allergen information for non-prepacked foods best practice
external_sources.supports: Use accurate current written information supported by a conversation. Communicate a customer requirement to the responsible trained adult. Never guess or promise that an unchecked item is safe.

What happened because of an action.

cases.text: You greeted a guest while an adult showed a prompt card.
cases.fact: The greeting used a visual prompt.
cases.next_step: Keep the greeting and the prompt in the review.

cases.text: The whole team finished, but your own task is not recorded.
cases.fact: The team result alone does not show your action.
cases.next_step: Find your work or an actual staff observation.
cases.staff_note: Do not assign an unobserved task to a learner.

cases.text: Feedback says the order was hard to hear.
cases.fact: The listener needed a clearer message.
cases.next_step: Try a written order or calm read-back.
cases.staff_note: Do not insist on speaking louder if another mode works.

cases.text: You practise a better greeting today.
cases.fact: Today’s rehearsal has its own date and context.
cases.next_step: Record it as practice and compare it carefully.

cases.text: The first chosen practice feels too much.
cases.fact: The learner needs a different way to take part.
cases.next_step: Use a quiet adult audience or point to a phrase.

cases.text: The new phrase still leaves the order unclear.
cases.fact: The observed practice has not solved the issue yet.
cases.next_step: Ask what was unclear and revise one step.
cases.staff_note: Record the real result rather than a success tick.

Access and practice
Supported: say one action with a prompt. Independent: link action, result and feedback. Aspire: explain how you could test a change.

Learners explain one action, its effect and support. Listen to actual feedback, then rehearse one chosen improvement with an adult or willing peer. The observer records what really happened in the rehearsal. If no past role exists, review today’s actual practice and mark the original service gap.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries
Dry role-play only. No real food, payment, personal customer details or external calls. No forced performance. A quiet one-to-one exchange is valid classroom participation.
Unconfirmed slot and in class alternative

Unconfirmed. No booking, invitation, placement or event date is asserted. A staff member is the in-class customer. Use a blank order slip, empty tray and an accessible response mode. No visitor or placement is required.
Assessment and feedback

The learner owns a specific action and acknowledges support. Link any claimed effect to a record. Keep the actual rehearsal response separate from past service evidence. Accept spoken, pointed, written or AAC responses. A polite script alone is preparation until it is used with an audience.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence banked). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Offer to the Communication portfolio
Explain a choice, listen to feedback and write or dictate a reflection. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own Communication portfolio; no criteria are assigned here.

Individual evidence key

The learner owns a specific action and acknowledges support. Link any claimed effect to a record. Keep the actual rehearsal response separate from past service evidence. Accept spoken, pointed, written or AAC responses. A polite script alone is preparation until it is used with an audience.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Supported communication can show progress.
Card B: Do not assign an unobserved task to a learner.
Card C: Do not insist on speaking louder if another mode works.
Card D: Never backdate the improved performance.
Card E: Offer choice and processing time.
Card F: Record the real result rather than a success tick.
Common misunderstandings
A team result does not show what each person did. Adult help should be recorded, not hidden. A rehearsal gives evidence of rehearsal, not proof that an earlier service action happened.
Teaching boundary
Dry role-play only. No real food, payment, personal customer details or external calls. No forced performance. A quiet one-to-one exchange is valid classroom participation.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.
